about: The Common Preface names no mystery of the day. After “through Christ our Lord” it turns to the angelic choirs' praise of God. Its opening sentence is built around “est”, which governs the construction “nos tibi grátias ágere”.

seg.nr: The priest parts his hands and holds them apart to the end of the Preface.

seg.tr: Truly it is right and just, fitting and leading to salvation, that we should give You thanks always and everywhere:

ex.w009: Latin “nos tibi grátias ágere” means literally “that we give thanks to Thee”. English likewise expands the construction as a clause.

seg.tr: Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: through Christ our Lord.
Through Him the Angels praise Your majesty, the Dominions adore it, and the Powers tremble before it.
The heavens, the heavenly Virtues, and the blessed Seraphim join in joyful celebration of Your majesty.
We beseech You to admit our voices to join theirs as we speak in humble confession:

ex.w052: The petition is put as a wish rather than a command.
ex.w055: A confession not of guilt but of praise — what the Sanctus is about to sing.
